title: We Mapped 115 Microservices for Our Coding Agents — Kamalakannan Nandagopal, Postman
talk_summary: Postman built an 'API context graph' mapping 115+ microservices, every endpoint, its implementing code line, and cross-service call/data flows, grounded in code or production traces, then exposed it to coding agents as a skill/context layer. They evaluated it against plain code search and Claude Code on real PRs, finding large quality and token-efficiency gains on API discovery, design/redesign, and impact assessment, but failures when the graph went stale.

takeaways.what_they_do: Catalog every service and endpoint, map each to the exact implementing code line and to cross-service callers/consumers and data flow, index it with an LLM, and require every node to be grounded in code or a production trace.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single data point that landed on the context graph always had to be grounded down in a hard truth
takeaways.numbers: 115 microservices mapped; 150+ services, thousands of endpoints

takeaways.technique: Evals mined from real PRs and design decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Take real merged PRs, record what the developer intended and the actual outcome, plus key design decisions, and turn each into a scored eval with the retrospective decision as ground truth; score 0-5 and track tokens per run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We mapped each and every one of them into an eval, and we mapped what the actual decision that was taken in retrospect as the ground truth
takeaways.numbers: Scored 0-5 plus exact token counts per run

takeaways.what_they_do: Use the graph to answer 'what downstream consumers are affected if this endpoint changes' and 'how is V2 used before designing V3', catching cascading effects at PR time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: almost 75% of the PRs had some effect on the APIs
takeaways.numbers: ~75% of PRs in top 10 repos affected APIs

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat graph staleness as the main failure mode: new consumers/APIs and removals must sync quickly, or results degrade and developers lose trust and stop using it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any delays in syncing your context graph with the ground truth uh creates gap in the result

takeaways.what_they_do: Plot quality score against exact tokens consumed per run, bucketing scenarios into efficient vs expensive, to justify the context layer on cost as well as quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also measured the exact amount of tokens it took for each of these runs
takeaways.numbers: Impact assessment: ~half to one-third the tokens vs pure code search

takeaways.what_they_do: Point the agent at the whole ecosystem to produce a 21-page report of dependency cycles, risky migrations, single points of failure, telemetry blind spots, with action items per role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it produced a 21-page engineering report going through every single weakness and points of vulnerability
